item.title: Amish Fall Farmhouse Experience at Old Windmill Farm — Fri Sep 11 — Old Windmill Farm
item.description:
An autumn afternoon in our farm kitchen. Join us as we bake bread, churn butter from our own cows’ cream, and press apple cider with a traditional hand-cranked apple press. Then sit down and enjoy all three together, with the freshly churned butter on the bread warm from the oven.
Press fresh cider with a traditional press Churn butter from our own cows’ cream Enjoy freshly baked bread Drink cider and eat bread with fresh butter A working farm kitchen, not a demonstration Advance reservations required

item.title: Evening Compline — Wed Sep 16, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: All We Have Is Her Gown: A Historic Pattern Drafter's Discoveries — Sun Sep 20, 2:00 PM — Historic Rock Ford
item.description: Historic Rock Ford’s Fashion of the 18th and 19th Century Lecture Series welcomes Mackenzie Sholtz as she presents “All We Have Is Her Gown: A Historic Pattern Drafter’s Discoveries.” Mackenzie Sholtz received a BA in Medieval Studies from Vassar College and a Certificate of Fashion Design from the Fashion Institute of Design and Merchandising in San Francisco. She worked in the San Francisco garment industry as a cutter, grader, and pattern drafter for a variety of smaller design houses. A move to South Carolina allowed her to volunteer in Sumter’s local museum which was expanding their educational program to include historic dress. This was the start to her creating her own pattern company focusing on 18th and 19th century women’s clothing based on extant garments in museum and private collections. item.title: Sparkdate: The Loxley's Social — Tue Sep 22, 6:30 PM — Loxley’s Restaurant
item.description:
Looking for a fresh, low-pressure way to meet single locals in person? Ditch the endless swiping and join us for a modern, structured dating experience designed to make real connection effortless, natural, and actually fun.
Check in with your host, grab a name tag, and jump right in—no app downloads or last-minute profile setup required. The evening unfolds in three distinct movements:
Movement 1: Guided Icebreakers. Start seated at a small table with an easy game designed to skip the awkward opening lines. Men rotate each round, ensuring you meet a fresh set of faces with every turn.
Movement 2: Open Mingling. The formal structure drops away. Move freely, chat with anyone you like, and build on conversations you started earlier. Because you’ve already broken the ice with most of the room, you avoid the cold-approach stress of a standard bar.

item.title: Beauty of Horror / Horror of Beauty: An Evening with Alma Katsu — Wed Sep 23, 6:00 PM — Zoetropolis Cinema Stillhouse
item.description:
Pocket Books is thrilled to invite you to an evening at Zoetropolis exploring the horrific beauty of ‘beauty horror,’ a subgenre that merges glamour and the grotesque to examine our culture’s obsession with aesthetic perfection.
Join us at 6pm for a talk with horror maven Alma Katsu, whose new book Incarnate offers a terrifying reimagining of The Picture of Dorian Gray for the internet age. You won’t want to miss our talk, followed by audience q&a and a book signing. At 7:30pm, we’ll enjoy a screening of Coralie Fargeat’s celebrated 2024 film The Substance. We will have books available for purchase at the event, but attendees are encouraged to order in advance!

item.title: Author Event with Peter Jaros — Sun Sep 13, 3:00 PM — Pocket Books Shop
item.description:
Join Franklin & Marshall professor Dr. Peter Jaros as he celebrates the publication of his new book The Corporate Forms of Antebellum U.S. Literature in conversation with his colleague Dr. Erik Anderson. Haven’t brushed up on your early 19th-century literature in a while? Don’t worry: no prior knowledge or reading required for this event.
You’ll get to learn about how in the early 19th century, the corporate form was still a wobbly category that writers used as a vehicle for imagining both personhood and politics in strange and surprising ways. And you’ll have the chance to talk about why anyone in 2026 would want to read books from the early 1800s & what exciting intersections there might be between law and literature.
